events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider [F3], so the fee can only arise through the rider-cancellation branch of NS-0, i.e. NS-4. NS-4 charges the $6.61 only when the rider cancels more than 3 minutes after matching; the system timeline records acceptance at 09:00:10 and cancellation at 09:03:09, i.e. 2 min 59 s (179 s) after matching [F3], which is inside the 3-minute free-cancellation window. The $6.61 on record [F6] was therefore not chargeable on the only applicable branch, and the trace's NS-4 ✗ element settles this. Under NS-2 that fee is refunded in full, as a voucher under NS-7. Both advocates converge on this and I adopt it.

The driver-side route to the fee also fails. NS-1 requires (i) an "I'm Here" tap, (ii) the driver within the pickup area at the tap, and (iii) more than 3 minutes' wait (≥ 3:01) within 200 m. The tap came at 09:03:00 at 39 m from the pickup [F5] and the rider cancelled 9 s later [F3]; cumulative GPS time within 200 m before cancellation was only 25 s [F2] and the driver was inside 200 m for just 5 s after tapping [F5], far below the >180 s threshold. NS-1(iii) therefore fails and the fee cannot be built on that branch either.

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" [F9] conflicts with the system records on presence and timing [F2][F4][F5]; system records (gps / timeline) override statements, so the statement cannot establish the waiting requirement of NS-1. The absence of any in-app messages [F8] means no chat-based consent or agreement (RD-5) is engaged, and the rider's "two minutes away" account is likewise uncorroborated by chat; neither point changes the outcome, which rests on the timeline and fare records [F3][F6].

No flag_account is warranted: NS-2's fraud add-on attaches only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup area, and here the GPS record places him 39 m away at the tap [F5] with a genuine recorded arrival at 09:02:40 [F4]. The rider's and driver's profile facts [F13][F14] are not used to decide the case.

Amount: the trace fixes the disputed item at the cancellation fee, $6.61 [F6][F3], refunded in full — 1 × $6.61 = $6.61 [F6][NS-2][NS-4][NS-7].

SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 screen: I read the complaint, the driver statement and the (empty) chat [F8][F9]; nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. The traffic and weather records show only ordinary speeds (band 4, 30–39 km/h), no incidents and fair weather [F10][F11][F12], so no safety escalation arises.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 rider cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; no account action against the driver.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee is invalid because the driver never satisfied the waiting requirement: he tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 (F5) and the rider cancelled at 09:03:09, i.e. only 29 s after the recorded arrival (F4) — far short of the required more than 3 minutes.
Cumulative GPS time the driver spent within 200 m of the pickup before cancellation was 25 seconds (F2), so the "waited > 3 minutes at the pickup" condition (NS-1(iii)) is not met.
Because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is not satisfied, the cancellation fee of $6.61 on record (F6) must be refunded in full to the rider.

The rider's cancellation came 2 min 59 s after acceptance (F3); even ignoring the driver's side entirely, this is within the 3-minute grace window, and the fee cannot be justified on a per-se late-cancellation basis either.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" (F9) is contradicted by the system timeline and GPS (F4, F5, F2) and by the absence of any in-app chat (F8); statements lose to GPS/timeline records, and there is no chat consent or agreement by the rider recorded anywhere.

No safety issue arises on this record: the traffic log shows only ordinary speeds on Anson Road (band 4, 30–39 km/h) with no incidents and fair weather (F10, F11, F12), and nothing in the chat or statement contains a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation.

weaknesses: The rider's own profile shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F13), which the other side will use to suggest a pattern of fee-dispute filings; this is a profile fact that cannot decide the case but colours credibility.

The rider cancelled the ride (cancelled_by = rider, F3), so if the driver had actually completed the NS-1 waiting requirements the fee would stand; the driver will lean on his statement (F9) that he waited over 6 minutes and called twice.

The driver did press "I'm Here" at a point 39 m from the pickup (F5) and did reach within 200 m (F2), so NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii) are arguably met — my case rests entirely on the timing element NS-1(iii), which the judge must find on F5/F4/F2.
There are no in-app chat messages at all (F8), so the rider's account of saying she was "two minutes away" is not corroborated by any chat record and cannot itself support a claim.

claims.assertion: This is a rider cancellation, so the only route to the $6.61 fee is NS-0/NS-4, and the rider cancelled 2 min 59 s after acceptance (09:00:10 → 09:03:09), i.e. within the 3-minute free-cancellation window.
Under NS-4 a cancellation must be charged only if it is made more than 3 minutes after matching; at ≤ 3:00 no fee is chargeable, so the $6.61 on record (F6) was not chargeable on this branch.

NS-1 does not save the fee either: the driver was within 200 m of the pickup for only 25 cumulative seconds before the rider cancelled (first inside 200 m at 09:02:40, cancellation 29 s later), far short of the >180 s required.

Even on the 'I'm Here' route, the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 and stayed within 200 m for only 5 more seconds before the rider cancelled at 09:03:09, so the >3-minute wait requirement of NS-1 fails.

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand" (F9) cannot support the fee: it is not rider consent and it is contradicted by the GPS/timeline records of a 25 s presence within 200 m, and the system records win over a statement.

The rider's stated reason ("I was two minutes away") has no in-app message behind it — the chat record contains no messages (F8) — so the fare consequence rests on the timeline alone, and the timeline shows she cancelled inside 3 minutes.

The fee should be refunded as a Ryde voucher under NS-7, and no account flag is appropriate against the driver: he did not mis-tap a false arrival sufficient to trigger NS-2's fraud add-on, and his profile shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days over 700 trips.

weaknesses: F1/F5: the driver did tap "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 only 39 m from the pickup and had physically arrived at 09:02:40 (F4), so the rider's "I was two minutes away" excuse does not make the driver look diligent but it does make him look already-present — the judge may read this as a genuine no-show setup rather than a fare grab.

F9: the driver's own statement asserts a 6-minute wait, which is directly contradicted by F2/F4 (25 s inside 200 m; cancelled 29 s after recorded arrival); if the judge treats this as a false arrival claim, NS-2's flag_account add-on is available against him, and my D7 request not to flag him is the weakest part of my brief.

F3: 09:03:09 is only 9 seconds past the 3-minute line and the complaint itself concedes the counterfactual of 179 s — a judge reading strictly could note that any GPS/timeline rounding places the cancellation close to the chargeable boundary, which cuts against the certainty of a full refund rather than for it.

points.response: Accepted — the fee can only arise through NS-0's rider-cancellation branch (NS-4); my case does not depend on NS-1 independently, because NS-4 itself decides whether the $6.61 is chargeable.
This agrees with C1/C4: the rider cancelled 2 min 59 s after acceptance (F3), within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 on record (F6) was not chargeable on the NS-4 branch.

Accepted and relied on: NS-1 cannot rescue the fee when the driver had only 25 cumulative seconds within 200 m before cancellation (F2) and cancelled 29 s after his recorded arrival (F4), far below the >180 s required.
Accepted: the "I'm Here" tap at 09:03:00 with only 5 more seconds inside 200 m before cancellation at 09:03:09 (F5, F3) fails NS-1(iii), so no fee can be built on the driver's arrival route either.

Agreed, and it goes further than the driver concedes: the 6-minute wait statement (F9) is contradicted by the system records (F2, F4), so under NS-2 the false "I'm Here" tap 39 m from the pickup (F5) with the rider charged anyway supports the refund.

The absence of any in-app messages (F8) cuts only against a chat-based theory; my refund rests on the fare record (F6) and the timeline (F3), which are system facts and are not displaced by the missing chat, and nothing in the record rebuts the rider's two-minutes-away account.

I take the full refund of $6.61 as conceded; as to the flag, NS-2 attaches flag_account only where the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him not within 200 m, and here F2/F5 place him inside 200 m at the tap, so my brief already asks only for a refund and I do not contest the driver-side flag point.

Conceded as to the timing element, but note it is fatal to the fee only on the NS-1 branch: the driver's "I'm Here" tap at 09:03:00 (F5) was followed by cancellation 9 s later (F3), so NS-1(iii)'s >180 s within 200 m is not met and the fee does not stand on that branch.
Conceded: F2 records only 25 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation, which is far short of the >180 s NS-1(iii) requires, so the waiting element cannot be made out from the system record.
I do not contest the refund of the $6.61 (F6); refund of the recorded fee is the correct result here, though it should issue as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 (NS-2), not as cash.

This is the strongest ground and I accept it: cancellation at 09:03:09 against acceptance at 09:00:10 on acceptance time is 2 min 59 s (F3), i.e. at or inside the 3-minute point, so no fee arises under NS-4 irrespective of the driver's position.

Agreed that F9 loses to the system records — my client's "6 minutes" claim is contradicted by F2 and F4 — but this cuts only against the fee, not against the driver's account being vexatious, and F8 confirms there is no rider message so no consent or agreement analysis (RD-5) is even engaged here.

Conceded — F10 shows only band 4 speeds, F11 no incidents and F12 fair weather, and nothing in F8/F9 reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so neither SAFE-1 nor SAFE-2 is triggered and no escalation is warranted.

I maintain my request that no flag_account issue against the driver: F5 shows he was genuinely 39 m from the pickup when he tapped and F4 shows a real 09:02:40 arrival, unlike the NS-2 scenario of a tap from outside the pickup area, and his F14 profile shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days.
